summary:
The Pitcairn Islands are a British Overseas Territory. Defence and external affairs are reserved to the United Kingdom, and United Kingdom domestic measures do not extend to Pitcairn of their own force; local ordinance governs.

Same-sex sexual activity has been legal in the Pitcairn Islands since 2001, so a visitor faces no criminalisation exposure on that ground.

The Pitcairn Constitution Order 2010 prohibits discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation, in force since 2010. The guarantee is constitutional rather than an offence provision, and it names sexual orientation and not gender identity, so a trans visitor has no express constitutional protection on gender-identity grounds.

Same-sex marriage has been legal since 14 May 2015. The Same Sex Marriage and Civil Partnerships Ordinance 2015 defines marriage as the union of two people regardless of sex, sexual orientation or gender identity, and the ordinance recognises civil partnerships performed outside Pitcairn. The ordinance was unanimously approved by the Island Council on 1 April 2015, signed by Governor Jonathan Sinclair on 5 May 2015 and published on 13 May 2015.

Adoption has been legal since 2015 and is open to married, unmarried and single people.

Military service falls under United Kingdom responsibility. None of the roughly 50 residents is known to be in a same-sex relationship.
tangentialFactors:
The territory's population of roughly 50 residents means there is no documented local pattern of anti-trans incidents to assess; the dossier records no such incidents.

The constitutional non-discrimination guarantee's coverage of sexual orientation but not gender identity places Pitcairn alongside jurisdictions whose written protections stop short of gender identity, even where relationship law is fully equal.
localsOnly:
Residents are covered by the Pitcairn Constitution Order 2010 non-discrimination guarantee on sexual-orientation grounds, and by the Same Sex Marriage and Civil Partnerships Ordinance 2015 for marriage and civil partnership recognition, including partnerships formed outside Pitcairn.

Adoption is available to married, unmarried and single residents alike under the regime in force since 2015.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the constitutional sexual-orientation guarantee has been invoked or adjudicated in any specific case is not sourced in the inventory.

No region-specific or trans-specific enforcement data, facility rules, or document-marker rules for Pitcairn are sourced; the national/territorial assessment rests on the constitutional and ordinance text alone.
